input.quote: B. By M&I. M&I shall indemnify Customer from, and defend Customer against, any liability or expenses arising out of or relating to (i) any claim by a third party that the Services or M&I's software infringe upon any United States patent, copyright or trademark of a third party
input.rationale: Section 14.2(B) does give us a Vendor IP indemnity (with defence) and 14.3 supplies notice, control-of-defence and cooperation procedures, so the core of the rule exists. However the fallback fails on two material terms: there are no infringement remedies (no obligation to procure continued use, modify or replace, and no refund if those are unavailable), and there is no super-cap — Section 13.4 expressly overrides every other provision and caps M&I's total liability, including the indemnity, at payments made in the three (3) months prior to the event, far below three times annual fees. We therefore target the fallback and make the shortest change: a new 14.2(C) carrying the procure/modify/replace-or-refund remedy and a 3x annual fees cap on Paragraph B, plus a conforming carve-out in 13.4 so the two caps do not conflict. The existing indemnity contains no Customer-modification, combination or specification exclusions, which is more favourable than the fallback permits, so we leave it unqualified. We do not pursue the preferred position here (affiliate coverage, Vendor data-breach and gross-negligence heads, and narrowing our own indemnity in 14.2(A)) as the fallback cure is sufficient.

proposal.summary: Add infringement remedies (procure/modify/replace, else refund) and a 3x annual fees super-cap for M&I's indemnity, carved out of the Section 13.4 cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept M&I's existing IP indemnity, but it must carry the usual infringement remedies and cannot be squeezed into the three-month liability cap, so we add procure/modify/replace-or-refund and a super-cap of three times annual fees, and carve that super-cap out of Section 13.4.

ops.text: Infringement Remedies; Indemnity Cap. If a claim described in Paragraph B(i) is made, M&I shall, at its option, procure for Customer the right to continue using the Services or M&I's software, or modify or replace the infringing item so that it is non-infringing, and if none of the foregoing remedies is reasonably available, M&I shall refund to Customer the fees paid for the infringing item. M&I's total liability under Paragraph B shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid by Customer under this Agreement.
